- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤-1.0) in recent days, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 3–5% for next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10% above prior peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment flips from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 5–8% for next 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +1, -1, +1), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment to forecast adjustment.
